title: fix(outbound): preserve angle-bracket placeholders in plain-text replies
body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes: default Telegram replies silently delete angle-bracket placeholders and generic type arguments, including the placeholders in OpenClaw's own `/model` help. ## User Impact User impact: instructions containing ``, ``, `List`, ``, and `` arrive intact without enabling rich messages. The shared plain-text sanitizer fixes all of its callers, not only Telegram. No configuration, SDK, or stored-state changes. ## Why This Change Was Made Preserve bare, unpaired, non-HTML angle names. Reuse the existing HTML element classification; standard element names still take precedence, as established in #152671. Attributed tags, paired custom/qualified tags, HTML-to-text conversions, numeric comparison handling, and malformed-tag stripping remain intact. Internal scaffolding and redaction are unchanged. The sanitizer is not a SecOps-owned or security-review-policy path on the tested base. The change is deliberately narrow rather than replacing the tag parser or relaxing internal-context stripping. ## Evidence Built baseline `8eb960d42a709610f5ad5ba587efa2ddcbeca367` and candidate `387bbe4c982a049a2a359bd5aa55d76dfc287fa8` ran isolated Gateways against Telegram's Test Server with real-user TDLib recording and a deterministic HTTP model. `richMessages` remained off. Bot identities are omitted. | Action | Before: user → reply | After: user → reply | Observation | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Placeholder prose | 73627 → 73628 | 73639 → 73642 | Before: `Run git checkout then npm install . Generic List and Map.` After: all placeholders and generic arguments retained. | | `/model` | 73629 → 73630 | 73643 → 73644 | Before: `/model -s` and `/think `. After: `/model -s` and `/think `. | | HTML and numeric control | 73631 → 73632 | 73647 → 73648 | Both: `x
next` displays as `x` then a newline and `next`; `a < b > c` and `x<5` remain literal. | The model replies arrived at 13.826s/118.867s before and 32.351s/114.805s after. The runs recorded 10/9 provider requests respectively, completed successfully, and released their Convex lease and private scratch state. An initial short scenario interrupted the first model turn with `/model`; the retained comparison uses separated turns instead. Telegram Web screenshots from one paired Test Server lease on those same builds: before 73678 → 73679 (9.505s), after 73687 → 73689 (158.231s). The native recording also captured `/model` 73694 → 73695 and the unchanged HTML/numeric control 73696 → 73697. The run completed, the browser session was terminated, and the Convex lease was released. **Before** ![Before: placeholder arguments disappear from the Telegram reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ab9660c-d7d9-4ce8-829c-bdeea546ae40) **After** ![After: placeholder arguments and generic types remain intact](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/781d3262-6837-43ce-8e4c-8393e6ef04dc) - Regression on baseline: **3 failed, 60 passed**. Candidate: **63 passed** in the sanitizer test file, including existing HTML, code, comparison, and internal-scaffolding controls. The shared `deliver-payload` contract test also passed. - Targeted Oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed. - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and baseline/candidate `pnpm build` completed in secretless Docker. The candidate build reported a non-fatal Control UI gzip budget violation (373495 B versus 373454 B); this diff does not change UI code. - Exact-head live OpenAI check through the built CLI completed using `gpt-4.1-mini`, returning `Run git checkout . Generic List.` The temporary key file and live-gate container were removed. - Cleanup: 24 task-created Telegram messages were deleted using recorded receipts; all deletion results were `ok`. The cleanup lease was released, the browser tab/session were closed, and all assigned proof ports are free. Merge danger: **two-way door**; reverting fully restores prior behavior without migrations. Blast radius: outbound channels using shared plain-text sanitization. Standard HTML markup keeps its previous handling; bare unknown angle names now remain visible rather than disappearing.
